findings.reason: §2 should extend `_path_differs_from_head`/`_path_has_a_staged_change` to return the blob ids it wants, or state why a fresh three-way comparator cannot reuse them, which changes §2's deliverable text.
findings.text: §2 says it will read staged paths with `git diff --cached --name-only` and compare each written path's content in HEAD, the index and the working tree, but that file already owns both comparisons: `_path_differs_from_head` (line 1482) is the HEAD↔worktree comparison and `_path_has_a_staged_change` (line 1743) is the HEAD↔index comparison run as `git diff --cached --name-only` — the exact form §2 proposes — while §1 itself cites the sibling `_restore_landing_writes` at the same file, so the plan searched this file and still proposes a parallel detector without citing either helper

findings.reason: routing the release commit through `_commit_landing_writes` puts §2's pre-stage and post-commit check in one place and collapses the plan's "two changes" to one, so the author must decide between extending the owner or forking the check twice, and a check written twice drifts.
findings.text: §2 names two commit sites to modify, `_commit_landing_writes` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1916) and the release-outcome commit at promotion_release.py:~635, but the release path is a second owner of the same landing-commit machinery: `_record_release_on_ledger` (promotion_release.py:569) runs its own `git add` / `git diff --cached --quiet` / `git commit --only -m "release(<run>): ..."` / `_restore_landing_writes` sequence (lines 611-650) instead of calling `_commit_landing_writes`, which is the owner exercised by all three other callers (promotion_gate.py:960, promotion.py:751, promotion.py:1350); the census of landing-commit sites is therefore one owner plus exactly this one duplicate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design adds no new module; §2's checks sit inline behind a small `landing_check` field on the landing result, so no substantial behaviour is spread over new wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 adds its check to two landing-commit sites, and the second, the release-outcome commit in promotion_release.py, is an inline duplicate of the landing-commit sequence owned by `_commit_landing_writes` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1916).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1811, cli_options 364, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §2 adds no CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family, so there is nothing to retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1 does search (it names `_restore_landing_writes` and its four rollback call sites with file:line, all verified present), but §2's planned readers reimplement comparison helpers that already exist in the same file it edits: `_path_differs_from_head` and `_path_has_a_staged_change`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — nothing new wraps existing machinery; the release-outcome commit does not forward to the landing-commit owner, it reimplements it, which is a duplicate rather than a wrapper.
